analysis.summary: Both Senegal and Iraq enter this Group I finale with 0 points and are definitively out of the top-two qualification spots, but Senegal retain a realistic path to the knockout round as one of the eight best third-placed teams — provided they win, ideally by a significant margin to improve a -3 goal difference. Iraq (GD -6) have nothing to play for in the table but can act as a spoiler. The quality gap is substantial: Senegal are guided by Sadio Mane and a squad built for the African continent's top tournament, while Iraq leaked seven goals across their two group matches, making this a strong home-on-paper fixture despite multiple Senegalese injury concerns.
analysis.home_form: Senegal lost both group stage matches: 1-3 to France (June 16, scored through Ibrahim Mbaye 90+5') and 2-3 to Norway (June 22, goals from Ismaila Sarr x2). They have shown attacking threat — scoring in both matches — but their defensive record (6 conceded in 2 games) is a concern. Sadio Mane provided the assist for Sarr's first goal versus Norway and remains fit and motivated as captain.
analysis.away_form: Iraq lost 1-4 to Norway (June 16, Aymen Hussein scored their only tournament goal) and 0-3 to France (June 22). They have conceded 7 goals in two matches and their only strike came in an already-losing position against Norway. Their squad showed limited ability to build sustained attacks against organised defences. Aymen Hussein — who scored 8 goals in qualifying and their sole World Cup goal — is reportedly a fitness doubt for this match.
analysis.h2h: This is the first senior international meeting between Senegal and Iraq. No prior head-to-head history exists. Senegal are unbeaten in two previous World Cup matches against AFC confederation sides: 2-2 vs Japan (2018) and 3-1 vs Qatar (2022).
injuries_news: Senegal GK Edouard Mendy (Chelsea) out with a ligament injury suffered vs Norway; Mory Diaw expected to start in goal.
Senegal attackers Nicolas Jackson, Ismaila Sarr, and midfielder Pape Gueye all absent from training ahead of the match and listed under medical supervision; their availability is unconfirmed.
Iraq striker Aymen Hussein (sole tournament goalscorer, 8 goals in qualifying) reportedly a fitness doubt.
key_factors: Senegal's strong motivation to win by a large margin: they need maximum points plus an improved goal difference to have any chance as best third-placed team; Iraq have zero table incentive.

Iraq's porous defence (7 goals conceded in 2 games) is highly vulnerable to Senegal's attacking unit even if Sarr and Jackson are limited or absent — Mane, Krepin Diatta, and Lamine Camara provide quality.
Simultaneous kickoff with Norway vs France means Senegal cannot manage the game based on other results; they must attack from the start.
Senegal's own defensive fragility (6 conceded in 2 games) and Mendy's absence in goal means Iraq can threaten on the counter despite their limited quality.
Toronto weather forecast: warm (~22°C), possible thunderstorms in early evening — unlikely to materially affect play at 19:00 UTC (3pm local).
This is the first-ever senior meeting between the two nations, removing any psychological head-to-head factor.
